subject:
Benchmark methodology & SLO follow-up 

 latency, throughput, streaming
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@edgefin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - benchmark methodology and SLOs

Hi Oliver - great to connect this morning. Thanks for walking us through EdgeFin's ingestion and streaming use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the performance/SLO qualification:

Summary of asks from your side:
- Target p95 latency (end-to-end generation) for single-stream interactive flows: <= 200ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens); <= 350ms for longer prompts (<= 512 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target for batch scoring: 5k requests/minute with 4k concurrency for embeddings/score jobs.
- Streaming requirements: chunked token streaming with <50ms inter-chunk latency; client needs partial tokens every ~100ms for a smooth UX.
- KV/cache behavior: warm KV expected for back-to-back sessions; cold-starts are rare.

What Redwood will deliver for the benchmark:
- Benchmark methodology doc (attached) detailing harness, measurement definitions (latency percentiles, tail behavior, warm vs cold), prompt sets, and reproducibility steps.
- Eval harness: a Dockerized runner + script to reproduce our numbers locally or in your environment.
- A seed prompt set (attached) representing your short/long prompt distributions plus streaming scenarios.

Proposed next steps:
1) We will share the methodology PDF and the prompt JSONL (attached) - please confirm these represent your workloads.
2) Rishi and team will propose a date for a 2-hour run (either on Redwood Dedicated or on your infra) and send an invite.
3) EdgeFin to provide a sample service account / test dataset (anonymized) and confirm whether test traffic will be routed through your VPC.
4) Post-benchmark: Redwood will produce a results report (latency p50/p95/p99, throughput curves, concurrency scaling) and recommend config (batching, quantization, kernel profile) to hit your SLOs.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-methodology-v1.pdf, edgefin-prompt-set-v2.jsonl

Let me know if I've missed anything. Happy to tighten the measurement definitions if you prefer different percentiles or histogram buckets.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Date: 2026-06-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - benchmark methodology and SLOs

Thanks Marissa - this looks good and captures the ask. Couple of clarifications from our side:

- The p95 targets you listed are correct for interactive UI flows; for API-to-API scoring (batch) our 5k requests/minute target is optimistic - we'd like to validate a burst to 8k/min to account for end-of-period jobs.
- For streaming, the UX team measures perceptual latency differently - can we add a metric for "time to first meaningful token" (TTFMT) and a 99ms budget for that on short prompts?
- We can provide a sanitized dataset and a short-lived service account. We will likely route test traffic through our staging VPC (details to follow).

Oliver

Date: 2026-06-28T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - benchmark methodology and SLOs

Thanks - adding a couple of technical notes so the benchmark is reproducible and apples-to-apples:

1) Measurement definitions (we included in the methodology PDF but calling out here):
   - p50/p95/p99 measured at the application layer (time from request received to last token emitted), plus kernel-level token generation latency where relevant.
   - Warm vs cold definitions: warm = KV cache primed with last 20 calls; cold = empty KV. Please confirm EdgeFin's typical warm-window.
2) Harness details:
   - We'll provide a Docker image that runs the harness (requests generator, streaming client, collector) and a results aggregator that outputs CSV + histogram PNGs.
   - For streaming, the harness will record time to first byte, time to first meaningful token (TTFMT), and inter-chunk latencies.
3) Reproducibility:
   - Seed RNGs and prompt ordering will be fixed; please commit the prompt-set file we sent to a shared Drive link to ensure exact reproductions.
4) Environment configs to report with every run: model name + revision, hardware profile (GPU type), kernel/quantization profile, concurrency config, batching window, and network RTT from client to endpoint.

Requests for EdgeFin before a run:
- Confirm warm-window semantics and provide a sample of traffic pattern (percentages for short/medium/long prompts).
- Confirm whether you prefer Redwood to run the benchmark on Dedicated infra (we can provision) or if you want us to run the harness in your staging VPC.

If you want, we can turn this into a short checklist in the HubSpot deal record so nothing gets missed.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
